boards.title: Your First Weekend at Sonoma State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A campus-based, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented, finding shared spaces, and sampling Sonoma State’s cultural and outdoor settings.

cards.title: Start at the Information Desk
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Student Center
cards.notes: Begin at the Student Center entrance and ask for directions or campus resources before setting out. It is the campus’s designated information point.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for campus wayfinding.
cards.evidence_claim: The Information Desk is inside the Student Center’s main entrance and assists visitors with questions and directions.
cards.access_notes: The Student Center posts operating hours; confirm them before going, especially during breaks.

cards.title: Settle into The Living Room
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Student Center, first floor
cards.notes: Use this shared lounge to pause with new classmates, choose a board game, or make a low-key plan for the rest of the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A casual indoor meeting point with board games.
cards.evidence_claim: The Living Room is a Student Center space for studying, playing, or relaxing with friends, and it has board games available.
cards.access_notes: Listed as a non-reservable public-use space for the campus community.

cards.title: Check the Student Involvement calendar
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Student Center, second floor
cards.notes: Look over the current events calendar and ask about ways to participate; choose an activity whose timing and access work for your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A source for campus events and involvement options.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Involvement hosts events and directs students to additional campus events through Seawolf Living.
cards.access_notes: Office address: Student Center, second floor. The page lists Monday–Friday office hours; event dates and access vary.

cards.title: Meet in Seawolf Plaza
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Between the Student Center and Recreation Center
cards.notes: Use the plaza as a simple meetup point, then look at LoboVision or sit together while the scheduled background music is playing.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus gathering space with LoboVision.
cards.evidence_claim: Seawolf Plaza sits between the Student Center and Recreation Center and has LoboVision; daily music is scheduled from 7:30 a.m. to 10 p.m., excluding closures and breaks.
cards.access_notes: Music is listed through 10 p.m.; check campus closure and break notices before planning an evening visit.

cards.title: Walk the Native Plant Garden trails
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Northeast campus, along Copeland Creek Trail
cards.notes: Take one of the named garden trails at an unhurried pace, read the interpretive features, and keep to maintained paths around the plant communities.
cards.short_summary: A demonstration garden with five named trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kenneth Stocking Native Plant Garden has 15 California plant communities, a butterfly-garden overlay, and five named trails.
cards.source_title: Native Plant & Butterfly Gardens | Geography, Environment, and Planning
cards.access_notes: Located on the northeast side of campus along Copeland Creek Trail; stay on marked paths and respect garden work areas.

cards.title: Pause at the Butterfly Garden benches
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · Off Copeland Creek Trail
cards.notes: Make this a quiet reset after the garden trails: sit at a bench, notice the pollinator plants, and leave the site as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A bench-lined garden beside the Native Plant Garden.
cards.evidence_claim: The Butterfly Garden is off Copeland Creek Trail, bordered by the Native Plant Garden and Lot G, with benches and nectar-rich plants that attract pollinators.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor setting; use the described trail access and respect plants and wildlife.

cards.title: See what is on at the University Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Art Building
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition listing before walking over, then give yourself time to view the displayed work and any accompanying gallery information.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery for contemporary art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Art Gallery presents exhibitions and public programs, including work by modern and contemporary artists and Sonoma State faculty and students.
cards.access_notes: The gallery lists Tuesday–Saturday, noon–4 p.m., during exhibitions only; confirm that an exhibition is open before visiting.

cards.title: Choose a Green Music Center performance
cards.subtitle: Saturday night · Weill Hall and lawn
cards.notes: Review the program, ticket details, and start time together; if a suitable show is scheduled, make it your planned evening destination rather than an assumption.
cards.short_summary: A campus performing-arts center with year-round programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Green Music Center is Sonoma State’s performing arts center and includes the 1,400-seat Weill Hall, whose rear wall can open to lawn seating.
cards.access_notes: Performances and ticket requirements vary. Consult the current event listing and ticket page before attending.

cards.entity_name: University Library, Jean and Charles Schulz Information Center
cards.title: Make a Sunday study plan at the library
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Jean and Charles Schulz Information Center
cards.notes: Pick a floor that matches your plan: use the first or second floor for conversation, or take independent work to the designated quiet third floor.
cards.short_summary: A weekend study stop with distinct quiet and group-study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Sunday hours of noon–7 p.m.; its first and second floors are open for individual and group study, while the third floor is quiet study space.
cards.access_notes: Current listed Sunday hours are 12:00–7:00 p.m.; verify holiday, break, and term-hour changes before going.

cards.title: Close with a walk by the University Lakes
cards.subtitle: Sunday late afternoon · Northwest of campus
cards.notes: Finish the weekend with a daylight walk to the lakes, staying on public paths and treating the water and surrounding habitat as a view rather than a recreation area.
cards.short_summary: A campus nature stop northwest of the academic core.
cards.evidence_claim: Sonoma State identifies the University Lakes as bodies of water northwest of campus and includes them among its campus nature-connection sites.
cards.access_notes: The campus nature-sites page says featured green spaces can be reached on foot from the campus center in 10 minutes or less; visit in daylight.
